stem:
Zaid connects the same nichrome wire to one cell for 5 minutes, then to two cells for 5 minutes. He also thinks about heat in an electric iron and heat at a hot plug.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Two cells produce more heat than one cell in the same time, and that heating is useful in an iron but harmful when a plug overheats.
Two cells always produce more heat than one cell, even when the connection times are different.
One cell produces more heat than two cells in the same wire over the same time.
Overheating at a plug is useful heating, just like the heat in an electric iron.

teacher.key_rationale: For equal duration on the same wire, two cells heat more than one; appliance heat can be useful while plug overheating is harmful. Ignoring equal time drops the comparison condition. One-cell-more reverses the relation. Calling plug overheating useful mis-scopes useful heating.
